topics.2: Australia's Place in the Global Economy

editions.summary: World share markets whipsawed this week, the US proposed new tariffs and oil stayed near US$90. At home, inflation and unemployment are both 4.9% and the dollar is near 66 US cents.
editions.big: shocks abroad (share-market falls, US tariffs, oil, stalled climate talks) reach Australia through financial contagion, the exchange rate and the terms of trade. With inflation and unemployment both at 4.9%, the RBA and the budget face a trade-off: a limitation of macro policy (Topics 2–4).

stories.title: World shares whipsaw: AI sell-off, record rebound, and a Fed leaning to more hikes
stories.lead: Global shares fell hard on 20 November, then bounced when Nvidia reinstated its CEO, while a US Fed official said several more rate rises are likely.
stories.q: Explain how a sharp fall in US share prices could affect the Australian economy. (4 marks)

stories.title: US proposes new 'excess capacity' tariffs on 14 economies
stories.lead: After an eight-month probe, the US trade office proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies on 25 November. Australia was not on the list.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain the effects of a tariff on domestic producers, consumers and the government. (6 marks)

stories.title: Oil swings around US$90 as the Hormuz disruption drags on
stories.lead: Brent hit its lowest close since 31 August, then jumped on 26 November as shipping problems continued. Fuel is a major driver of Australian inflation.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain why a supply disruption in oil can cause a large rise in price. (4 marks)

stories.title: COP31 ends with no deal after the longest climate summit on record
stories.lead: Talks in Antalya, co-presided by Australia's Chris Bowen, ended on 22 November with no agreement, after two days of overtime.
stories.q: Explain why international agreements to reduce emissions are hard to reach. (4 marks)

stories.title: Australian dollar hits an 11-month low as iron ore and copper slide
stories.lead: The AUD fell to about 66 US cents, wiping out its 2026 gains, as commodity prices dropped and markets priced US rate rises against RBA cuts.
stories.q: Explain how a fall in iron ore prices could lead to a depreciation of the Australian dollar. (4 marks)

stories.title: Inflation hits 4.9% as unemployment rises: stagflation fears grow
stories.lead: Inflation hit a three-year high in October just as unemployment jumped to 4.9%.
stories.q: Explain why inflation and unemployment rising together creates a dilemma for policy makers. (5 marks)

stories.title: RBA expected to hold in December as the budget is asked to share the load
stories.lead: The cash rate is 4.85% after a 6–3 vote on 3 Nov. Chalmers says December's MYEFO will show net savings.
stories.q: Assess the effectiveness of monetary and fiscal policy in reducing inflation while unemployment is rising. (6 marks)

editions.summary: China's economy is losing steam, US interest rates are heading up and trade barriers are at a record. At home, the dollar has slipped to about 67 US cents and unemployment has jumped to 4.9%.
editions.big: weaker Chinese demand, higher US interest rates and rising protection (Topic 1) reach Australia through the terms of trade, the exchange rate and borrowing costs (Topic 2). With unemployment rising and inflation still above target, the RBA faces a trade-off: a limitation of monetary policy (Topics 3 and 4).

stories.title: Trade barriers hit a record as leaders meet at APEC
stories.lead: The WTO says governments brought in more new trade restrictions in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, just as Australia's Prime Minister joined APEC leaders in Shenzhen.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain the effects of a tariff on domestic producers, consumers and the government. (6 marks)

stories.title: China's slowdown deepens as key October data all miss forecasts
stories.lead: Factory output, retail sales and investment all grew more slowly than forecast in October. China is Australia's largest trading partner and the main buyer of our iron ore.
stories.q: Explain how weak consumption and investment in China could affect Australia's terms of trade. (4 marks)

stories.title: US bond yields jump as markets bet on a Fed rate hike
stories.lead: US government bond yields had their biggest weekly rise since April 2025 as markets priced in a likely Federal Reserve hike in December. Australian long-term yields rose to match them.
stories.q: Why might rising US yields push up Australian borrowing costs even if the RBA does nothing? (4 marks)

stories.title: The Aussie dollar slides to 67 US cents as the rate gap narrows
stories.lead: The dollar lost 1.4% in a week as rising US yields and fading hopes of another RBA hike narrowed the interest-rate gap that had supported it. A Wall Street sell-off then dragged commodities lower.
stories.q: Explain how a depreciation of the Australian dollar could affect inflation and the RBA's decisions. (4 marks)

stories.title: RBA minutes reveal a 6–3 split, and a December pause is expected
stories.lead: Minutes released on 17 November show six board members voted to lift the cash rate to 4.85% and three wanted to hold at 4.60%. CommBank economists expect no change in December.
stories.q: Using the November RBA minutes, explain the trade-off the board faced between reducing inflation and supporting employment. (5 marks)

stories.title: Unemployment jumps to 4.9% as real wages fall for a fourth quarter
stories.lead: Higher rates are cooling the labour market, and pay is still not keeping up with prices.
stories.q: Distinguish between nominal and real wage growth, and explain how faster wage growth could affect inflation. (4 marks)

stories.title: Is the AI investment boom running out of steam?
stories.lead: Analysis: ABC's Ian Verrender compares the AI rush with earlier booms and crashes, and says it looks shaky.
stories.q: Explain how a sharp fall in global share markets could affect the Australian economy. (4 marks)

editions.summary: Oil has had its steepest weekly fall since COVID, China's exports are booming, hot US inflation has lifted the US dollar and markets bet the RBA has finished raising rates. This week shows how global prices and money flows reach Australia.
editions.big: global prices and money flows (oil, China's exports, US interest rates) reach Australia through the terms of trade, the exchange rate and inflation (Topics 1 and 2). The RBA must then weigh a weaker dollar and sticky inflation against falling confidence: a limitation of macroeconomic policy (Topics 3 and 4).

stories.title: Oil has its steepest weekly fall since COVID, but Hormuz risks remain
stories.lead: Brent fell about 16% in the week to 6 November on hopes of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and has drifted lower since. Shipping attacks continue, so the price could turn quickly.
stories.q: Using a demand and supply diagram, explain how reopening the Strait of Hormuz would affect the world price of oil, and outline one effect on Australia's inflation rate. (4 marks)

stories.title: China's exports jump 35% and its trade surplus tops US$1 trillion
stories.lead: China's exports surged in October while its consumer prices rose just 0.7%. Beijing also extended its pause on an extra 24% tariff on US goods ahead of an expected Trump–Xi meeting.
stories.q: Explain how China's reliance on export-led growth could increase protectionism in the global economy. (4 marks)

stories.title: Hot US inflation puts a Fed rate hike on the table
stories.lead: US consumer prices rose faster than expected in October. Markets now fully price a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rise in December, with knock-on effects for global capital flows and the Australian dollar.
stories.q: Explain how a rise in US interest rates could affect the Australian dollar and inflation in Australia. (4 marks)

stories.title: COP31 admits 1.5°C will be missed and bets on electrification
stories.lead: The UN climate summit in Antalya, co-hosted by Türkiye and Australia, accepts for the first time that warming will exceed 1.5°C. Its main idea is a voluntary push for electricity to supply 35% of the world's energy by 2035.
stories.q: Assess the effectiveness of voluntary international agreements in addressing global environmental problems. (6 marks)

stories.title: Has the RBA finished raising rates? Surveys sag as the AI boom adds pressure
stories.lead: A week after the fifth rise of 2026, weak consumer and business surveys have markets betting the RBA is done. The RBA's chief economist says the global AI investment boom could keep rates higher for longer.
stories.q: Explain how a surge in data-centre investment could affect inflation and interest rates in Australia in the short run and the long run. (4 marks)

stories.title: The Australian dollar slides as the US dollar hits a 19-month high
stories.lead: Hotter US inflation lifted the US dollar to its strongest since April 2025 and pushed the AUD to about 68 US cents.
stories.q: Explain how a depreciation of the Australian dollar could affect inflation and the RBA's monetary policy decisions. (4 marks)

stories.title: Households and firms pull back as home lending suffers a record fall
stories.lead: Consumer confidence is at a four-year low and new home lending has had its biggest fall on record.
stories.q: Explain how a fall in housing lending can affect economic growth and the distribution of wealth in Australia. (4 marks)

editions.summary: Brent crude fell almost 9% on Thursday to about US$95 after nearly reaching US$118 last week, China's factories are shrinking and the RBA has lifted the cash rate to 4.85%. This week shows how events overseas reach Australia.
editions.big: events overseas (an oil supply shock, weaker Chinese demand, higher world interest rates, tariffs) reach Australia through prices, the terms of trade, the exchange rate and interest rates (Topics 1 and 2). The RBA must then weigh imported and home- grown inflation against slowing growth: a limitation of macroeconomic policy (Topics 3 and 4).

stories.title: Oil peaks near US$118, then falls almost 9% in a day to US$94.62
stories.lead: Brent rose 13.6% in October as tanker attacks peaked, then fell 8.7% on 5 November as traders bet a Democratic Congress will push for an earlier end to the Iran war. Hormuz is still disrupted.
stories.q: Using an AD/AS diagram, explain how a sustained rise in world oil prices affects inflation, output and unemployment in Australia. (6 marks)

stories.title: China's factories slip back into contraction as export orders fall
stories.lead: China's official factory survey fell below 50 in October and services and construction contracted too: a warning sign for Australia's largest export market.
stories.q: China buys about a third of Australia's goods exports. Explain how a slowdown in Chinese manufacturing could affect Australia's terms of trade and current account. (5 marks)

stories.title: Democrats take Congress, but America's tariffs are likely to stay
stories.lead: Voters punished President Trump over the cost of living in the 3 November midterms. Trade lawyers say the tariff wall will not come down, because the powers Trump now uses do not need Congress to sign off each year.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain the effects of a tariff on consumers, domestic producers and the government in the importing country. (6 marks)

stories.title: Rates rise worldwide as government debt piles up
stories.lead: Investors want higher returns to lend to governments, pushing up interest rates around the world. An ABC analysis argues that deficits, not just the size of spending, add to inflation.
stories.q: Discuss how rising global interest rates could affect Australia's economy and federal budget. (6 marks)

stories.title: The RBA lifts the cash rate to 4.85% and calls inflation 'home-grown'
stories.lead: On Melbourne Cup Day the RBA raised the cash rate by 25 basis points, an 18-year high, by six votes to three. It judged inflation broad-based and capacity pressures tighter than it thought.
stories.q: Explain TWO factors that the RBA's Monetary Policy Board considered in deciding to raise the cash rate to 4.85% in November 2026. (4 marks)

stories.title: The dollar holds near 70 US cents as rates rise and commodities mix
stories.lead: The AUD barely moved on a day of big market swings: higher rates support it, while mixed commodity prices pull the other way.
stories.q: Explain two factors that influence the value of the Australian dollar, and how a change in its value affects the current account. (5 marks)

stories.title: Housing downturn deepens as David Jones collapses and NAB cuts 2,500 jobs
stories.lead: Home values fell for a seventh month, and high rates are now hitting retailers and banks.
stories.q: Explain how rising interest rates affect house prices and consumer spending through the wealth effect. (4 marks)

stories.title: Goods trade surplus jumps to $2.8 billion as imports fall
stories.lead: Australia's surplus on goods trade widened sharply in September: exports of fuels, metals and meat rose while imports fell, led by a big drop in gold.
stories.q: Explain how a larger goods surplus affects Australia's current account deficit. (4 marks)

stories.title: Diesel squeeze: Australia pays billions more to find new suppliers
stories.lead: Australia is the world's largest buyer of seaborne diesel. War in the Gulf and drone strikes on Russian refineries have reshaped the global diesel trade.
stories.q: Explain how a rise in world diesel prices affects Australia's balance on goods and its CPI. (4 marks)

stories.title: US tech giants push for trade retaliation over Australia's news levy
stories.lead: Meta, Google and other platforms say the News Bargaining Incentive breaches the Australia–US Free Trade Agreement, when the US has already put tariffs on Australian goods.
stories.q: Discuss the risks to the Australian economy of the US retaliating over the news levy. (6 marks)

stories.title: Data centres could use twice the power of every home in Sydney
stories.lead: A NSW inquiry warns the data-centre boom could swamp the grid and derail emissions targets, and that nobody knows the true demand.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain how rapid data-centre growth could affect electricity prices. (4 marks)

editions.summary: Inflation hit 4.3%, oil is near US$115 and unemployment is rising. The RBA decides on Melbourne Cup Day whether to raise rates again.
editions.big: a supply shock pushes prices up and growth down together (stagflation), forcing a hard trade-off between inflation and unemployment: a key limitation of macroeconomic policy (Topic 4).

stories.title: Inflation jumps to 4.3%, and fuel leads the way
stories.lead: Annual CPI inflation rose to 4.3% in September, up from 4.0% in August. Underlying inflation also edged up, strengthening the case for a fifth RBA rate rise today.
stories.q: Distinguish between headline and underlying inflation, using data from the September 2026 CPI release. (4 marks)

stories.title: Missile strike on Saudi refinery keeps oil near US$115
stories.lead: A Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery has renewed fears about Middle East oil supply. Crude is staying at levels that feed inflation around the world, including in Australia.
stories.q: Draw an AD/AS diagram to show how a sustained rise in world oil prices affects output and the price level in an oil-importing economy. (4 marks)

stories.title: One oil shock, three answers: Canada hikes, Europe and NZ hold
stories.lead: Central banks faced the same energy-price shock this week but reached different conclusions, showing how policy depends on each economy's inflation, growth and expectations.
terms: interest rate differential oil price shock
stories.q: Explain why central banks might respond differently to the same rise in world oil prices. (4 marks)

stories.title: No recession in sight, but the jobless rate is heading up
stories.lead: At Senate estimates, RBA officials said none of their indicators point to a recession. They still expect unemployment, already 4.7%, to keep rising as higher interest rates slow the economy.
stories.q: Explain why the RBA may need unemployment to rise in order to reduce inflation. (4 marks)

stories.title: Markets all but certain of a Melbourne Cup Day rate rise
stories.lead: After the hot inflation result, markets put the chance of a 25 basis point rise on 3 November at up to 90%. All four major banks now expect the cash rate to go from 4.60% to 4.85%.
stories.q: Explain how an increase in the cash rate is transmitted through the economy to reduce inflation. (5 marks)

stories.title: Chalmers rules out a new fuel discount and promises savings
stories.lead: After inflation hit 4.3%, the Treasurer said the budget cannot afford another fuel excise cut and flagged savings in December's mid-year update.
stories.q: Explain how a fuel excise cut could reduce measured inflation in the short term but work against the RBA over time. (4 marks)

stories.title: The Australian dollar climbs as markets bet on an RBA hike
stories.lead: The hot inflation result lifted expectations of a November rate rise and pushed up the Australian dollar. Against the NZ dollar it hit its highest level since early 2013.
stories.q: Explain how a widening interest rate differential between Australia and New Zealand affects the value of the AUD and the external sector. (4 marks)

editions.summary: Wednesday's CPI is the last big number before the RBA's Melbourne Cup Day decision on 3 November, with oil near US$114, house prices falling and unemployment at 4.7%.
editions.big: an oil supply shock pushes prices up and growth down together (stagflation), so the RBA must weigh inflation expectations against rising unemployment: a key limitation of macro policy (Topic 4).

stories.title: Wednesday's CPI will set up the RBA's Melbourne Cup Day decision
stories.lead: The ABS releases the September-quarter CPI on Wednesday 28 October, six days before the RBA meets. Underlying inflation is expected above the RBA's forecast, with fuel the biggest single driver.
stories.q: Distinguish between headline and underlying inflation, and explain why the RBA focuses on underlying measures. (4 marks)

stories.title: Houthi strikes on Saudi oil keep crude near a five-month high
stories.lead: Yemen's Houthis said on Saturday they had attacked Saudi oil facilities and airports, adding to fears about supply from the world's largest crude exporter just as oil sits at its highest in five months.
stories.q: Using a supply and demand diagram, explain why a disruption to Saudi oil supply could cause a large rise in world oil prices. (4 marks)

stories.title: The RBA says rate rises are “not quite yet” done
stories.lead: Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said on Sunday that demand is still running ahead of what the economy can supply. Markets now price roughly a 61–67% chance of a fifth rise on Melbourne Cup Day, 3 November.
stories.q: Explain why the RBA is concerned about rising inflation expectations and how monetary policy can respond. (6 marks)

stories.title: House prices fall for a sixth month, with a record quarterly drop
stories.lead: Two measures agree the slide is deepening: Cotality has national values down six months in a row, and Domain's median house price had its biggest quarterly fall on record as rate rises bite.
stories.q: Explain how rising interest rates affect the distribution of wealth in Australia. (4 marks)

stories.title: Tariffs, retaliation, then subsidies: Canada shields steel and autos
stories.lead: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford announced a joint package for steel and auto firms hit by 50% US tariffs, while the White House quietly reshuffled which Canadian goods it taxes.
stories.q: Explain the effects of a tariff on domestic consumers, domestic producers and the government. Use a diagram. (6 marks)

stories.title: Challenger rejects a Japanese-owned insurer's takeover bid
stories.lead: The board of annuities provider Challenger rejected an $11.80-a-share offer from TAL Dai-ichi, owned by Japan's Dai-ichi Life, but is still talking with the bidder. It is a live example of foreign direct investment.
stories.q: Explain how a completed takeover would affect Australia's financial account now and its current account in later years. (4 marks)

stories.title: Coalition costs $31b of cuts as a MYEFO downgrade looms
stories.lead: The Opposition has released PBO-costed savings of $31.3b over four years to pay for tax changes, while Treasurer Chalmers says December's MYEFO will show softer growth and slightly higher unemployment.
stories.q: Discuss whether fiscal policy should be tightened to support the RBA's efforts to reduce inflation. (8 marks)

editions.summary: Oil is above US$110 and the IEA says it won't settle down soon. China grew on exports, NAB is cutting jobs, and the RBA could raise rates again on Melbourne Cup Day.

stories.title: China grows faster, but exports are doing the heavy lifting
stories.lead: China's economy grew 4.5% over the year to the September quarter, beating forecasts. The growth came from selling goods overseas, not from spending at home, and that is creating tension with China's trading partners.
stories.q: Define trade surplus. (2 marks)

stories.title: Oil above US$110, and the IEA says don't expect relief in 2027
stories.lead: The International Energy Agency (IEA) is the world's main energy watchdog. Its head, Fatih Birol, says he sees no credible path to normal oil markets next year, because conflict in the Middle East keeps supply at risk.
stories.q: Using an AD/AS diagram, explain how a rise in global oil prices affects inflation and economic growth in an oil-importing economy such as Australia. (6 marks)

stories.title: The US scraps planned 100% tariffs on Russia's oil buyers
stories.lead: A US law was about to put 100% tariffs on goods from the five biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas, a group that includes China and India. Days before the tariffs were due to start, the US President used his power to waive them, saying the main aim was to bring energy prices down.
stories.q: Outline two reasons other than protecting local industry that a government might impose tariffs. Use this story as an example. (4 marks)

stories.title: BHP's copper output falls 19% and its iron ore prices drop
stories.lead: BHP is Australia's biggest miner. In the September quarter it produced much less copper than expected, and the price it received for iron ore fell. Its results give an early sign of how Australia's export income is tracking.
stories.q: Explain how a fall in iron ore prices affects Australia's terms of trade and current account balance. (4 marks)

stories.title: Australian lamb could face new US tariffs
stories.lead: US sheep farmers want protection from imported lamb, most of which comes from Australia and New Zealand. A US trade body is now running a safeguard investigation that could end in higher tariffs on Australian lamb.
stories.q: Using a diagram, explain the effects of a US tariff on Australian lamb exporters, US producers and US consumers. (6 marks)

stories.title: A Swedish investor agrees to buy Cleanaway for $9.3 billion
stories.lead: Cleanaway, Australia's biggest waste and recycling company, has agreed to be bought by EQT, a Swedish private equity firm. The deal values Cleanaway at about $9.3 billion including its debt. When a foreign company buys an Australian business, it shows up in the balance of payments. W H Y T H I S M AT T E R S When a foreign investor buys a controlling stake in an value of Cleanaway, including its debt Australian company, it counts as foreign direct investment (FDI). The purchase brings money into Australia and is recorded as a credit in the financial account.
stories.q: Discuss the costs and benefits of foreign ownership of essential-service companies in Australia. (6 marks)

stories.title: NAB to cut 2,500 jobs as fears of a downturn grow
stories.lead: NAB, one of Australia's big four banks, will cut up to 2,500 jobs by mid-2027 and says rapid technological change is the reason. Other large employers are cutting jobs too, which raises the risk that job losses feed on themselves.
stories.q: Using the NAB job cuts and the September Labour Force data, distinguish between structural and cyclical unemployment. (4 marks)

stories.title: Consumers grow gloomier as petrol passes 240c a litre
stories.lead: Consumer confidence has fallen again, and Australians now expect prices to keep rising quickly. That matters because what people expect about inflation can help make it happen.
stories.q: Explain how rising inflationary expectations can make inflation harder to bring down. (4 marks)

stories.title: Will the RBA raise rates again on Melbourne Cup Day?
stories.lead: The Reserve Bank has raised the cash rate four times this year, most recently to 4.60% in September. Its meeting minutes show it was not prepared to wait for inflation to fall on its own. Economists disagree about whether it will raise rates again on 3 November. T H E D E B AT E Case for a rise (ANZ's forecast): inflation is still too cash rate, after a 0.25 high, inflation expectations are rising, and the minutes say further increases are possible. Case for holding (CBA's forecast): unemployment is rising, house prices are falling, and earlier rate rises take time to affect the economy. 2–3% the RBA's inflation target
stories.q: Evaluate how effective monetary policy can be in reducing inflation that is caused by rising global oil prices. (8 marks)
